values.input_schema: {"type":"object","required":["problem","audience","category","store"],"properties":{"problem":{"type":"string","minLength":5,"description":"The painful problem the app solves, in one sentence, as the people who have it would say it"},"audience":{"type":"string","minLength":3,"description":"Who has the problem every day"},"category":{"type":"string","minLength":2,"description":"The store category the app would sit in, for example Health & Fitness or Food & Drink"},"store":{"enum":["app-store","google-play"],"description":"Which store the app launches in first"},"competitors":{"type":"array","maxItems":5,"items":{"type":"string","minLength":2},"description":"Competing apps the person already knows, by name"}}}
values.job: Take a consumer app idea from a painful daily problem to a live subscription app: confirm that apps in the category already earn and that creators already post about the problem (stop if not), record the top 3 competitors' onboarding beats, paywall, price and growth channels from the person's own screenshots, write an onboarding that follows the winning order of beats in original words and design, end it with a paywall that states price, trial and cancellation plainly, publish a store page whose subtitle says what the app does, then run five growth channels (creators paid per post, influencers on a capped cost per 1,000 views, faceless slideshows, founder-made posts, paid ads after organic winners) with disclosures, and review installs, trials, paid users and revenue every week. Every number comes from a tool call or the person's own store and payment dashboards; where there is none, the answer is "no data". The AI drafts; the person owns the developer account, the payment setup and every contract, approves every word, and submits.
values.produces: Each Monday: installs, trials, paid users and revenue by channel, with the channel that won and why; the weekly numbers are a build-in-public post.
values.source: {"from":"X posts","author":"Ernesto Lopez","url":"https://x.com/ErnestoSOFTWARE/status/2014110519913857122","name":"Ernesto Lopez, 'I built 10 apps in 10 months' guide (X article), and his post on cooking apps and generated cooking reels (https://x.com/ErnestoSOFTWARE/status/2115897827775988205)","note":"His claims, not checked here: about $800,000 a year from 10 apps; his first app made $20,000 in its first 30 days from 2 viral videos; a recipe app at about $1M a month; a paid influencer at $1 per 1,000 views capped at $1,000; creators paid $15 a post with bonuses from $150 at 100K views to $800 at 1M. His 8 steps: validate the niche (a daily painful problem, apps already earning over $10K a month, creators already posting), build fast with AI coding tools, borrow the onboarding and pricing of the best competitors (he says he means their structure, not a literal copy, with the inside of the app original), a hard paywall at the end of onboarding, a minimal store page (clear name, a subtitle that says what it does, 3 to 5 big-text screenshots, a simple description), then five growth channels: creators, influencers, faceless slideshows with one style or character, founder-led posts, paid ads. NOT ADOPTED, with the reason: (1) copying a competitor's screens, words or design, which is copyright and trade-dress infringement, so only the order of beats is reused and every word and screen is new; (2) a paywall that hides how to close it, restore a purchase or cancel, or that charges before a clearly stated trial end, which breaks App Store guideline 3.1.2 and consumer-protection rules on subscriptions, so the paywall states price, period, trial end and how to cancel; (3) creator and influencer posts without an ad disclosure, which breaks endorsement rules, so every paid post carries one; (4) hiring a minor to send 100 cold messages a day, so outreach is done by the person or an adult they contract, one message at a time and within each platform's messaging rules."}
values.title: Validate and launch a subscription app
